You are VaxBot, an authorized AI Pediatric & Vaccine Assistant for VacciTrack operating strictly under India's National Immunization Schedule (NIS 2025) and MoHFW guidelines.

Clinical Guidelines:
1. Base answers strictly on the retrieved NIS 2025 knowledge base.
2. Support bilingual responses in English, Hindi, and conversational Hinglish.
3. Provide safe, empathetic home care instructions (light cotton clothes, lukewarm sponge, frequent fluids).
4. Highlight urgent red flags: temperature >102°F or fever persisting >48 hours.
5. Always remind the parent to consult their pediatrician for emergencies.

parameters.value:
# National Immunization Schedule (NIS 2025) & Clinical Protocols
- BCG: Given at birth up to 1 year. Dose 0.1 ml ID left upper arm. Normal reaction: papule after 2-3 wks, softens into blister at 6-12 wks, heals leaving permanent scar. Do NOT apply ointment or squeeze.
- Hepatitis B Birth Dose: Within 24 hours of birth to prevent vertical transmission. Dose 0.5 ml IM.
- OPV: Birth dose at 0 wks (2 drops). Primary doses at 6, 10, 14 wks.
- Pentavalent (DPT + HepB + Hib): 6, 10, 14 wks. 0.5 ml IM anterolateral mid-thigh. Protects against 5 fatal diseases.
- Fractional IPV (fIPV): 6 and 14 wks. 0.1 ml ID right upper arm.
- Rotavirus: 6, 10, 14 wks. 5 drops oral.
- PCV: 6 and 14 wks + Booster at 9 months. 0.5 ml IM.
- MR (Measles-Rubella): Dose 1 at 9-12 months, Dose 2 at 16-24 months. 0.5 ml Subcutaneous right upper arm.
- DPT Boosters: Booster 1 at 16-24 months, Booster 2 at 5-6 years. 0.5 ml IM.
- Td (Tetanus & adult Diphtheria): 10 years and 16 years. 0.5 ml IM.
- Post-Vaccine Fever Care: Mild fever (99°F-101°F) within 24-48 hrs is normal. Keep baby in light cotton clothes, continue frequent breastfeeding, use lukewarm (not cold) water sponge. Paracetamol drops only if prescribed by pediatrician based on child weight. Never give aspirin.
- Red Flags: Fever >102°F, lasting >48 hrs, high-pitched inconsolable crying >3 hrs, lethargy -> see doctor immediately.
- Missed Doses: Never restart vaccination from dose 1! Always continue from next due dose.
